referenceCard.title: Conditionals

subtitle: A program that decides. First True wins; indentation shows what belongs.

teach.body:
A comparison is a question with a True or False answer: 5 > 3 is True, 5 == 3 is False. == asks 'equal?'; = stores a value. Others: != (not equal), <, <=, >, >=.

if condition: runs the indented lines below it only when the condition is truthy. % gives a remainder, so n % 2 == 0 asks 'is n even?'.
teach.title: Asking a question

teach.body:
if a: … elif b: … else: … is one chain. Python checks a; if it is truthy, that block runs and the rest of the chain is skipped. Only if a is falsy does it check b, and so on. else runs when no earlier test was truthy. So at most one block in a chain runs, and order matters.

Two separate if statements are two separate questions; both can run.
teach.title: Chains: first True wins

teach.body:
and / or return one of their operands, not necessarily True or False. x and y returns x when x is falsy, otherwise y; x or y returns x when x is truthy, otherwise y. An if tests the truthiness of the result. not x returns a bool with the opposite truthiness. The right side is skipped when the left decides the result.

Falsy values include False, 0, 0.0, "", empty collections and None. name or "guest" returns "guest" for any falsy name, including 0 and None. 3 or 0 gives 3. 0 and 5 gives 0.

Indentation is the structure. Lines indented under if belong to it; the first line back at the left edge is outside and always runs.
